faults.description: Administration PC has a /25 mask instead of /24, so its own subnet range stops at 192.168.10.127 and it cannot reach the gateway.
faults.symptom: PC-ADMIN-1 can reach no host outside 192.168.10.1-126 and `ipconfig` shows a 255.255.255.128 mask.
faults.hint_1: Compare the mask on the PC against the department subnet in the brief.
faults.hint_2: A /24 is 255.255.255.0. A /25 halves the usable range.

faults.description: Faculty subinterface carries the Students address 192.168.20.1, duplicating VLAN 20's gateway and leaving VLAN 30 with no gateway at all.
faults.symptom: VLAN 30 PCs have no default gateway reachable; R1 has the same address on Gi0/0.20 and Gi0/0.30.
faults.hint_1: Read every subinterface address on R1 and compare to the subnet table.
faults.hint_2: Gi0/0.30 is the Faculty gateway. It should be .30.1, not .20.1.

faults.description: PC-STUDENT-2 is a VLAN 20 host but its access port is in VLAN 30.
faults.symptom: PC-STUDENT-2 gets a Faculty-range DHCP address or none, and `show vlan brief` lists Fa0/3 under VLAN 30.
faults.hint_1: Match each access port to the department its PC belongs to.
faults.hint_2: PC-STUDENT-2 sits in VLAN 20. Check Fa0/3 on SW-ACCESS.

faults.description: VLAN 10 is never created on the distribution switch, so its SVI cannot come up and Administration traffic has no L2 path.
faults.symptom: `show vlan brief` on SW-DIST has no VLAN 10 entry; the Vlan10 interface stays down/down.
faults.hint_1: List the VLANs on both switches. A VLAN present on one is not enough.

faults.description: PC-FACULTY-1's access port is in VLAN 20 (Students) instead of VLAN 30 (Faculty).
faults.symptom: `show vlan brief` lists Fa0/5 under VLAN 20; PC-FACULTY-1 gets a Students address or none.
faults.hint_1: Check which VLAN each Faculty port actually belongs to.
faults.hint_2: Fa0/5 on SW-ACCESS should be in VLAN 30.

faults.description: The access switch trunk uses native VLAN 1 while SW-DIST uses 99, so untagged frames land in different VLANs on each side.
faults.symptom: `show interfaces trunk` reports a native VLAN mismatch; some untagged traffic is black-holed or leaks between VLANs.
faults.hint_1: Compare the native VLAN on both ends of the uplink.

faults.description: The dist-to-access trunk does not allow VLAN 30, so Faculty traffic cannot cross the uplink.
faults.symptom: `show interfaces trunk` on SW-DIST omits VLAN 30 from the allowed list; Faculty hosts cannot reach their gateway.
faults.hint_1: An allowed-VLAN list that omits a department silently deletes it.
faults.hint_2: VLAN 30 is missing from the trunk's allowed list.

faults.description: The default route points at 10.0.0.6, an address that does not exist on the /30 transit link.
faults.symptom: `show ip route` shows the default via 10.0.0.6; nothing off-campus is reachable.
faults.hint_1: Check that each next hop is on a connected subnet.
faults.hint_2: The /30 is 10.0.0.0/30: usable addresses are .1 and .2, not .6.

faults.description: Faculty PC's default gateway is 192.168.30.254, which no device owns, instead of the router subinterface .1.
faults.symptom: PC-FACULTY-1 pings its own subnet but nothing beyond it.
faults.hint_1: A gateway must be an address that exists on the router.

faults.description: The Students DHCP pool declares network 192.168.200.0/24 — a typo — so the pool cannot serve 192.168.20.0/24 clients.
faults.symptom: `show ip dhcp pool` shows the wrong network; Students PCs get no address without a static fallback.
faults.hint_1: Compare each pool's network statement with the subnet table.

faults.description: No address is excluded for the router's own .1 in the Administration pool, so DHCP can hand the gateway address to a PC.
faults.symptom: No excluded-address line in the running config; a client may receive 192.168.10.1 and duplicate the gateway.
faults.hint_1: Reserve infrastructure addresses before the pool can lease them.
faults.hint_2: 192.168.10.1 belongs to R1 and must be excluded.

faults.description: The Students DHCP pool omits `dns-server`, so Students PCs receive no resolver while other departments do.
faults.symptom: `show ip dhcp pool STUDENTS` has no DNS option; Students PCs get an address but cannot resolve names.
faults.hint_1: Every pool must hand out a resolver, not just an address.

faults.description: The Administration PC's access port is administratively shut down, so the PC has link at the NIC but no switch port.
faults.symptom: `show interfaces status` on SW-DIST lists Fa0/1 as disabled/notconnect.
faults.hint_1: A port that is administratively down cannot pass traffic.
faults.hint_2: Fa0/1 on SW-DIST is shut down.

faults.description: SSH is configured on the vty lines but no local username exists and `login local` is absent, so remote management is impossible or falls back to an unauthenticated path.
faults.symptom: `show run | section line vty` shows `transport input ssh` with no `login local`; a console-less login cannot authenticate.
faults.hint_1: SSH needs an authentication source on the vty lines.
faults.hint_2: Create the local user and add `login local` to `line vty 0 4`.

faults.description: SW-ACCESS has no enable secret, so privileged EXEC is reachable without an encrypted password.
faults.symptom: `show running-config` on SW-ACCESS has no `enable secret` line; `enable` prompts for nothing.
faults.hint_1: Privileged mode must require an encrypted password.
